hypothesis: A deterministic iteration-boundary root-volatility latch allocates equal aggregate nodes more usefully than Stockfish's native time manager, a uniform budget, and a shuffled allocation.

frozen_policy.native_control: Stockfish nodestime=1, remaining_moves=50, clock secant-calibrated before oracle scoring
frozen_policy.uniform_control: same observed mean nodes, selected before oracle scoring
frozen_policy.causal_ablation: shuffle the adaptive per-position node-budget distribution

gates: candidate option-off matches reference on all three exact normalized transcripts
two independent internal adaptive processes match moves, volatility flags, histories, and aggregate nodes within one percent
adaptive, native, uniform, and shuffled aggregate nodes are each within one percent
adaptive-vs-native, adaptive-vs-uniform, and adaptive-vs-shuffled bootstrap mean lower bounds are above zero
adaptive wins are not fewer than losses in all three comparisons
promotion: Passing advances only to equal-node and fixed-time games; deep-oracle evidence alone cannot establish strength.
rollback: Reject or redesign the latch if reproducibility, compute matching, native-TM, uniform, or shuffled causal gates fail.
